result.title: Post-Audit Mirage: Identifiability Limits of Offline Agent Verification
result.comment: Accepted at the Workshop on Who Verifies the Agents? Toward Reliable Agent Development, NeurIPS 2026. 17 pages. Code: https://github.com/beingamanforever/Post-Audit-Mirage
result.summary: Offline tests can fail to reveal whether an agent update will remain safe after deployment. We operationalize this post-audit mirage using matched safe and harmful lifecycles that expose identical verifier-visible evidence while an isolated scorer records opposite deployment truth. Our theorem applies standard observational-equivalence and indistinguishability ideas to this executable audit boundary and states the resulting error-abstention tradeoff. The Post-Audit Mirage benchmark makes that boundary executable across authorization, scheduling, and shared-capacity environments. IdentifiedRangeMonitor uses fresh group-labelled harm outcomes to return deploy, hold, cannot determine, or unsupported. Experiments show that monitoring can recover the missing distinction in favorable settings but may remain undecided for rare groups, small effects, or missing observations. Verifier-agent evaluation must therefore test both calculation validity and whether the available evidence supports the deployment decision.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究离线审计无法区分部署后安全与否的「审计后幻象」问题，给出观测等价下的误差—弃答权衡定理，并构建覆盖授权、调度、共享容量环境的基准及带「无法判定」输出的 IdentifiedRangeMonitor。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「现有证据是否足以支持判定」与不可辨识性分析，可能为核查 LVR 中多 latent 假设、视觉证据筛选及何时应弃答/停止提供概念工具；但对象是 agent 安全审计而非多模态推理状态，需较多核查才能迁移。
